test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 15, 10 and 30 days, respectively. In how many days can A do the work if he is assisted by B and C on every 3rd day?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 10, 30) = 30 units.

Efficiencies: **A** = 2, **B** = 3, **C** = 1.

Work in a 3-day cycle: (A) + (A) + (A+B+C) = 2 + 2 + (2+3+1) = 10 units.

Total days for 30 units = (30 ÷ 10) × 3 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A works alone on the 1st and 2nd days. A, B, and C work together on the 3rd day.

⇒ Work on Day 1 (A) = 2 units

⇒ Work on Day 2 (A) = 2 units

⇒ Work on Day 3 (A + B + C) = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 units

⇒ Total work in 1 cycle (3 days) = 2 + 2 + 6 = 10 units

⇒ Number of cycles required = Total Work ÷ Work per cycle = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 cycles

⇒ Total time = 3 cycles × 3 days/cycle = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In problems involving **alternate days** or specific assistance patterns, calculate the total work done in one complete **cycle** and then divide the total work by this value.

Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.</p
